newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian firms see Q2 profits higher - ABS.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian firms see Q2 profits higher - ABS.

text.p: Australian businesses expect profits to rise 7.8 percent in the June quarter from the previous quarter, the Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday.
This compared with an expected fall in profits of 2.9 percent in the March quarter and a rise of 9.6 percent in the corresponding quarter of last year, the bureau said.
Selling prices are expected to rise just 0.3 percent in the June quarter, although this is higher than the expectations for the three previous quarters, which were each 0.1 or 0.2 percent.
But the price expectations were weaker than the 0.7 percent expectation recorded a year ago for the previous June quarter.
Businesses expected sales to rise 1.6 percent in the June quarter, compared with the unusually weak expectation of 0.4 percent that had been held for the March quarter.
A year ago, sales had been expected to rise 2.3 percent in the June quarter of 1996.
The bureau's survey differs from other business expectations series in that it calculates the volume of expected movements as well as direction.
It does this by asking respondents for the size of expected movements and then weighting results for the respondent's size.
Each survey, conducted in the middle month of each quarter, asks for expectations for the following quarter.
